g.text: I'm Saransh Singh, a final-year Electronics and Communication Engineering student at
DCRUST Murthal, India, and Cybersecurity Lead for the 2026 batch. I started on the blue-team
side — logs, kill chains, indicators — and now spend most of my time on offence: mobile
application testing, hardware security and drone authentication.
I learn by building. A BLE HID framework on an ESP32-S3, an authentication scheme that
rebuilds its key from silicon instead of storing one, a scanner that keeps working inside
RASP-protected Android apps. Each one ends with a write-up that says what works, what
doesn't, and what I would do differently.
Offensive tooling, mobile app assessments, ESP32 firmware and the occasional desktop environment.
Android internals, BLE, physical unclonable functions, and the places where hardware and app
Report quality, reproducible testing, and the habit of proving a finding rather than assuming it.
